opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; working groups must have diverse mix of members at different career stages, institutions and international participation.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing up to £30,000 towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups of 8-15 individuals who analyse existing data using a hypothesis and question-led approach.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: Up to £500 per year for 10 years; £3,500 claimable in year 1 (first five years' funding) and an additional £3,500 in the sixth year.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with at least 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices that improve learners' experience and promote excellence in ecological education, providing up to £5,000 towards evidence-based learning.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants

amount.raw: Grant awards of up to £20,000 can be claimed from the applicant.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20,000 towards placements in a distinctly different discipline or sector for up to 12 months, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world; BES funding cannot be used towards completion of an undergraduate or master's degree or funded fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, supporting work that advances ecological science.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication activities.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £250 is available for virtual conferences/courses; a maximum of £500 is available for events in person.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (registered on a postgraduate research degree programme); work or study at a university or research institution.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to present their work at workshops and conferences; awarded on a lottery-based system.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering travel, registration, food and accommodation up to £1,000, awarded via a lottery-based system.
